milestone: M58 Bounded Autonomous Product Loop Drive

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves product-continuation target construction from caller-owned glue into Rust drive/advance authority while preserving explicit authorization and bounded route steps.
Lets the explicit agent loop consume one persisted product-continuation continuation route without requiring the caller to assemble source/run target JSON.
Keeps route-kind validation, provenance freshness, replay identity, and task.run delegation in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or scheduler.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive and headless.run.advance can derive one product-continuation admission or run target from the current persisted route evidence under explicit derivation authorization.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M58.1 could execute product-continuation routes only when the caller supplied the full admission or run target object; the runtime still did not own target construction from its own checkpoint evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled autonomous caller would still need external target-construction glue and could make stale or mismatched target choices outside Rust route authority.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M57.1 admission, M57.2 run execution, and M58.1 explicit-target drive forwarding because this phase derives the target inside the runtime from persisted route evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive and headless.run.advance request envelopes are extended; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, preview, dashboard, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime now validates a derived target authorization, checks the current persisted route kind, reconstructs the existing M57 target from bounded ledger/checkpoint evidence, and validates replay identity before returning persisted results.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can advance the product-continuation loop by authorizing derivation instead of interpreting ledger evidence and assembling target objects itself.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the M58 shift from explicit route execution to runtime-owned bounded product-continuation drive target derivation.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive and headless.run.advance accept exactly one product_continuation_derived_target per bounded advance
admission derivation is allowed only from a persisted admit_product_continuation_task_explicitly route and requires bounded continuation goal input
run derivation is allowed only from a persisted run_product_continuation_task_explicitly route with current continuation task/run provenance
derived targets delegate to the existing M57 admission/run implementation instead of adding a new execution path
replay validates the derived request identity against subordinate admission or run evidence and rejects mismatched replay requests
behavior tests cover derived admission success, duplicate-free replay, derived run execution, and mismatched derived replay denial
no new JSON-RPC method, report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, preview, inspection, dashboard, provider expansion, workspace mutation expansion, or VSIX-owned policy is introduced

ledger and RPC outputs exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment values, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, tokens, and secrets

behavior_evidence: derived drive admission and run behavior test
Rust workspace compile and test validation
safety_boundary: requires explicit product-continuation target derivation authorization
requires matching persisted headless run product-continuation route boundary
derives one admission or one run target per advance
delegates execution only to existing headless.continue_once and task.run authority
stores bounded identifiers and SHA-256 fingerprints only
non_goals: no unbounded loop or background scheduler
no automatic product continuation without explicit authorization
rejected_alternatives: leaving product-continuation target assembly outside the runtime
adding a derived-target inspection or preview report
auto-running multiple product-continuation steps in one drive
moving route policy into the VSIX
technical_debt: The runtime file remains large; extraction should remain a later behavior-preserving refactor.
This phase still advances one product-continuation route step per advance rather than an unbounded product loop.
next_capability_rationale: If this phase is accepted, M58 can close out and the next milestone should move to the next distinct runtime capability rather than adding another product-continuation wrapper.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M58.2 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for a runtime behavior phase. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
